edges.label: CIA convened and sponsored the panel, and concealed that sponsorship
edges.note: The panel was convened by the Office of Scientific Intelligence. The CIA's own history states that any mention of Agency sponsorship of the panel was forbidden.

edges.label: CIA convened and staffed the January 1953 scientific advisory panel
edges.note: Convened by the Office of Scientific Intelligence under H. P. Robertson; the panel recommended debunking and the monitoring of civilian UFO groups.

edges.label: Ruppelt attended the panel as Blue Book director and later described it
edges.note: Ruppelt was present at the January 1953 sessions in his official capacity and published his account of the panel's function three years later.

edges.label: Durant was panel secretary and wrote the proceedings record
edges.note: Durant's memorandum of 16 February 1953 to the Assistant Director for Scientific Intelligence is the only substantive record of what the panel actually discussed.

edges.label: Chaired the CIA-convened panel of January 1953
edges.note: Robertson chaired the panel at CIA's request; the report is the founding document of American UFO information management.

edges.label: Robertson chaired the panel
edges.note: Robertson, a Caltech physicist and CIA consultant who had directed the DoD Weapons Systems Evaluation Group, chaired the 14-18 January 1953 sessions and signed the report.

edges.label: CIA convened the panel that recommended debunking
edges.note: The Robertson Panel was convened by CIA's Office of Scientific Intelligence, placing the recommendation inside the intelligence community rather than the Air Force.

edges.label: Hynek presented to the panel but was not a member
edges.note: The Air Force's scientific consultant briefed the CIA-convened panel; the formal membership was Robertson, Alvarez, Berkner, Goudsmit and Page.

edges.label: Panel recommendations became binding Air Force regulation
edges.note: AFR 200-2 was issued 26 August 1953 and revised 12 August 1954, restricting public release on unexplained cases to the bare fact of ATIC analysis — the debunking recommendation converted into internal law within months of the panel reporting.

edges.label: Debunking recommended as a security measure
edges.note: The Robertson Panel's January 1953 recommendation for a mass-media debunking programme is the documented point where concealment becomes an influence operation.
